answer: Each epoch a head may publish a finished answer it will never claim. A later claim is paid only if a jury finds it strictly better than one such waiver from an unrelated head, and that waiver is then spent. The scarce input is the waived success itself: unprintable, unlendable, gone on use, and a farm's own waivers count as one identity, so a tenth head must wait on a stranger. Honest heads stop waiving to an address that gathers them. In the karst of the waiver roll a sprig of yarrow marks each spent entry, and the copper seal on it is burned.
